title: Robustness to model misspecification
question: BayesPlanner assumes the public default parameters. How badly does it do when the true world differs?

players.bayes_true: BayesPlanner(seed, device=cuda:2, config=true perturbed config) (extra control)
players.oracle: oracle_manifesto + balance.policy_planner on the true state (run_batch)

metric_definitions.gap_bayes_minus_oracle: paired E_bayes − E_oracle in the same perturbed world
metric_definitions.misspec_cost: E_bayes − E_bayes_true (same world and streams; negative = misspecification hurts)
metric_definitions.sensitivity.max_abs_delta_gap: max over the parameter's arms of |mean delta_gap| (primary ranking)
metric_definitions.sensitivity.max_misspec_cost: max over the parameter's arms of −mean misspec_cost (secondary ranking)

leak_check.rule: costs identical; dynamics arms: whole initial observation identical; generation arms: only ['free_stats', 'inter_edges', 'regions'] (realised public census / free statistic) differ; no key named like ['dirichlet_concentration', 'exposure_prob', 'mean_degree', 'sensitivity', 'social_step', 'threshold', 'zealot_fraction'] except regions[*].mean_degree (realised census); public_config(obs) == default public config

test_families.delta_gap: 15 non-default arms: (E_bayes − E_oracle)_arm − (…)_default, Wilcoxon signed-rank, Holm
test_families.wins_bayes_vs_oracle: 16 arms: exact McNemar bayes vs ORACLE, Holm
test_families.misspec_wins: 15 arms: exact McNemar bayes vs bayes_true, Holm

deviations: z × 1.5 = 1.2375 is invalid (z must lie in [0, 1]); replaced by z = 0.9125 (margin 1 − z halved) and z = 0.7375 (margin × 1.5). The plan's z × 0.5 = 0.4125 is kept.
Extra control arm bayes_true (BayesPlanner told the true parameters), beyond the plan's ORACLE comparison.
Electorates drawn on the GPU (generation='device'); parity uses the canonical CPU draw.
BayesPlanner games run 4 at a time in threads of one process (one GPU process at a time).
